fact: 1930年6月17日，胡佛总统签署斯穆特—霍利关税法，对超过2万种进口商品提高关税。应征税进口商品的平均税率从1929年的40.1%升至1932年的59.1%，为1830年（61.7%）以来最高；自由与应税合计税率从1929年的13.5%升至1933年的19.8%。该法案1929年5月28日已在众议院以264对147通过。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Smoot–Hawley Tariff Act
sources.quote: Signed into law by President Herbert Hoover on June 17, 1930 ... the act raised tariffs on over 20,000 imported goods in an effort to shield American industries from foreign competition during the onset of the Great Depression ... The dutiable tariff rate peak of 1932 was 59.1%, second only to the 61.7% rate of 1830. ... The average tariff rate, which was applied on dutiable imports, increased from 40.1% in 1929 to 59.1% in 1932 (+19%).

fact: 斯穆特—霍利法案引发报复：1930年5月加拿大率先对16种商品加征新关税，这些商品约占美国对加出口的30%；古巴、墨西哥、法国、意大利、西班牙、阿根廷、澳大利亚、新西兰与瑞士随后也实施报复性关税。美国对提出抗议国家的出口下降18%，对实施报复国家的出口下降31%；德国则发展出一套通过清算（clearing）进行的贸易体系。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Smoot–Hawley Tariff Act
sources.quote: Some countries protested and others also retaliated with trade restrictions and tariffs. American exports to the protesters fell by 18%, and exports to those which retaliated fell by 31%. ... In May 1930, Canada, the most loyal trading partner for the U.S., took action by imposing new tariffs on 16 products which accounted altogether for approximately 30% of U.S. exports to Canada. ... Germany developed a system of trade via clearing.

fact: 1930年12月10日，纽约布朗克斯南大道分行出现挤兑，起因是当地一名小商人散布该行拒绝其售股的谣言；到中午聚集2万至2.5万人，需警察维持秩序，当日2500至3000名储户提走200万美元，但到场约7000名储户中的大多数最终仍把钱留在银行。次日，董事会在担心全面挤兑的情况下决定关门，请纽约州银行监管人约瑟夫·布罗德里克接管资产。该行股价当年最高91.50美元（1928年历史高点231.25美元），消息公布后由11.50美元跌至3.00美元（最低2.00美元）。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Bank of United States
sources.quote: On December 10, 1930, a large crowd gathered at the Southern Boulevard branch in the Bronx seeking to withdraw their money ... By midday, a crowd of 20,000 to 25,000 people had gathered and had to be controlled by the police, and by the end of the day, 2,500 to 3,000 depositors had withdrawn $2,000,000 from the branch. However, most of the 7,000 depositors who came to withdraw their money left their assets in the bank. ... The next day, fearing a run on the bank, the directors decided to close the bank and asked the New York Superintendent of Banks, Joseph Broderick, to take over the bank's assets.

fact: 美国银行倒闭前，四家纽约大银行曾于1930年11月24日宣布合并计划，12月8日因无法就担保该行存款达成一致而放弃；随后大华尔街银行拒绝提供3000万美元过桥贷款，救助失败。该行存款总额在1930年10月17日至12月11日间从2.12亿美元降至1.6亿美元。在1930年11月至12月倒闭的608家银行中，美国银行一家占全部5.5亿美元存款损失的三分之一；仅12月一个月全国就有300多家银行倒闭。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Bank of United States
sources.quote: On December 8, 1930, unable to agree on merger terms, the plan was dropped ... Without the necessary $30 million bridge loan, the bank could not be saved. ... gross deposits in the bank had dropped from $212 million to $160 million between October 17 and December 11. ... Among the 608 banks that closed in November and December 1930, the Bank of United States accounted for a third of the total $550 million in deposits lost ... More than 300 banks nationwide failed in that single month.

fact: 纽约市面包零售价1930年1月至9月为每磅8.6—8.7美分，10月至12月降至8.5美分；1931年1月进一步降至8.0美分。也就是说，1930年食品零售端的通缩在下半年才刚开始，全年跌幅不足3%，真正的价格崩塌发生在1931年。这与「1930年物价已经崩了」的直觉不符。

fact: 联邦农业委员会依1929年《农业销售法》设立，由原联邦农业贷款委员会改组而成，拥有5亿美元周转基金，通过收购并储存余粮与棉花来稳定价格、促进农产品销售。玉米价格从1929年每蒲式耳1.43美元跌至1932年的0.31美元；1929至1932年美国家庭平均收入下降40%。农业委员会在1933年3月被行政命令改为农场信贷管理局。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Federal Farm Board
sources.quote: The Federal Farm Board was established by the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1929 ... with a revolving fund of half a billion dollars to stabilize prices and to promote the sale of agricultural products. The board would help farmers stabilize prices by buying and holding surplus grain and cotton in storage.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Depression in the United States
sources.quote: Crop and livestock prices plummeted — corn fell from $1.43 per bushel in 1929 to just $0.31 by 1932. ... Between 1929 and 1932, the income of the average American family was reduced by 40%.

fact: 1930年美国没有联邦存款保险：储户在银行倒闭后只能等待清算分配，或依靠清算所与州政府安排的「以存款为抵押借款」方案。美国银行倒闭后，纽约清算所银行提出向该行储户贷出其存款的50%，部分储户直到12月23日才开始拿到贷款，许多人排队数小时仍未能办理。联邦存款保险公司要到1933年《格拉斯—斯蒂格尔法》才设立。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Bank of United States
sources.quote: members of the New York Clearing House Association offered to lend Bank of United States depositors 50% of their deposits. ... Some depositors started to receive their loans on December 23, 1930, and The New York Times reported that throngs of depositors lined up to receive their loans, many arriving hours before the branches opened, and many were turned away because they could not be served by the end of the day.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Black Tuesday
sources.quote: The Glass-Steagall Act of 1933 instituted a series of banking reforms, including separating commercial and investment banking, and created the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, which protected consumer deposits in the event of a bank failure.

fact: 1930年纽约州的银行监管结构是双轨的：州注册银行由州银行监管人（Superintendent of Banks）接管与清算，国民银行由联邦货币监理署管辖，两者都没有存款保险兜底。美国银行是州注册银行，因此其关闭与资产接管由州监管人执行；联邦储备系统在1930年并未承担最后贷款人角色，救助依赖私人银行团的过桥贷款，而该贷款被拒绝。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Bank of United States
sources.quote: the directors decided to close the bank and asked the New York Superintendent of Banks, Joseph Broderick, to take over the bank's assets. ... Broderick tried to arrange a merger with three other banks, but the big Wall Street banks refused to help. Without the necessary $30 million bridge loan, the bank could not be saved.

fact: 斯穆特—霍利法案生效后贸易额急剧萎缩：美国进口从1929年的44亿美元降至1933年的15亿美元（降66%），出口从54亿美元降至21亿美元（降61%）；自欧洲的进口从1929年13亿美元降至1932年3.9亿美元，对欧出口从23亿美元降至7.84亿美元。1929至1934年间世界贸易总额下降约66%。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Smoot–Hawley Tariff Act
sources.quote: U.S. imports decreased 66% from $4.4 billion (1929) to $1.5 billion (1933), and exports decreased 61% from $5.4 billion to $2.1 billion. ... Imports from Europe decreased from a 1929 high of $1.3 billion, to $390 million in 1932. U.S. exports to Europe decreased from $2.3 billion in 1929 to $784 million in 1932. ... Overall, world trade decreased by some 66% between 1929 and 1934.

fact: 关税战催生了绕开关税的贸易安排：德国因应美国及各国的关税壁垒，发展出一套通过清算（clearing）进行的双边贸易体系——两国以记账对冲的方式结算进出口，避免用稀缺的外汇支付关税与货款。加拿大则在1930年5月对美国16种商品加税后，把部分采购转向英帝国其他成员。这类「清算协定、易货、转口」安排是1930年关税战下真实存在的贸易替代路径，而非理论推演。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Smoot–Hawley Tariff Act
sources.quote: Nations other than Canada that enacted retaliatory tariffs included Cuba, Mexico, France, Italy, Spain, Argentina, Australia, New Zealand, and Switzerland. France and Britain protested and developed new trading partners. Germany developed a system of trade via clearing.

fact: 1929年6月，伯宰（Clarence Birdseye）把公司与专利以2200万美元卖给Postum公司与高盛交易公司，Postum随后更名为通用食品公司并成立Birds Eye冷冻食品公司。1930年3月6日，该公司在马萨诸塞州斯普林菲尔德的零售店启动销售试验，报纸整版广告列出26种产品（含18种切块冷冻肉、菠菜、豌豆、浆果、蓝点牡蛎与鱼柳）；最初参与门店为10家（另一来源记18家）。双带式急冻机（美国专利1,773,079）与多板式急冻机（1927年专利）是这项技术的基础。
